core_obligations: Reduce to a single combinatorial complex: evaluate the complex of presheaves at an object V and split it according to the composite morphism phi : V -> U, writing the degree p part as a direct sum over phi of Z[S_phi x ... x S_phi] with S_phi the disjoint union of the sets Mor_phi(V, U_i), so that it is enough to treat one fixed set S (proof lines 1642-1681).

Exhibit a nullhomotopy: for the complex Z[S] <- Z[S x S] <- Z[S x S x S] <- ... fix s in S and define the chain map K sending n_{(s_0, ..., s_p)} to n_{(s, s_0, ..., s_p)}, and check by direct computation that K is a nullhomotopy for the alternating-sum operator delta (proof lines 1687-1694).
Conclude exactness in negative degrees for every S_phi, hence exactness of the complex of abelian presheaves in all degrees except zero (proof lines 1681-1698).
proof_roadmap: Evaluate at V and reorganise the complex as a direct sum indexed by the composite morphisms V -> U (proof lines 1642-1669).
Rewrite each summand as the tensor-like complex of one set S_phi, reducing the claim to a purely combinatorial statement (proof lines 1670-1687).
Give the explicit homotopy K and verify it is a nullhomotopy of delta, which yields exactness in negative degrees (proof lines 1687-1698).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a family U = {U_i -> U} with all fibre products existing, the resulting chain complex of abelian presheaves Z^bullet_U is exact in every degree except zero (statement lines 1628-1638). The proof is a genuine computation in two stages: first the complex is evaluated at an object V and decomposed into a direct sum indexed by the composite morphisms V -> U, which reduces everything to the complex Z[S] <- Z[S x S] <- Z[S x S x S] <- ... for one set S; then an explicit chain map K : n_{(s_0, ..., s_p)} -> n_{(s, s_0, ..., s_p)} is written down and checked to be a nullhomotopy of the alternating-sum operator (proof lines 1687-1694). The author's proof carries a typographical slip in the displayed definition of delta, where the sign is written (-1)^p instead of (-1)^i; it is reproduced verbatim and not corrected. The claim is H2: a concrete homotopy, no citations beyond the definition.
